sections.title: Content
sections.text:
The matrix claims a global lock order. I will check that claim against the inlined actions and the lock, quota, and foreign-key code they call.review: grok/grok-4.7 findings:4

1. PostgreSQL wait-for cycle. The new-version upload takes `CAS` and only then updates the file row, so matrix point 2 is false. `UploadFileAction.php:92` takes `TS`, `:98` calls `BlobStore::commit` (`BlobStore.php:70` `BlobLock` / `pg_advisory_xact_lock`) before `commitNewVersion` updates the node at `:211`. A same-storage schedule with identical bytes deadlocks: Rename holds file `N` and waits for parent `P` (`RenameNodeAction.php:41` then `:46`); new-file upload holds `P` (`:280`) and waits for that `CAS`; new-version upload holds that `CAS` and waits for `N`. PostgreSQL aborts one transaction with `40P01`.

2. Purge locks the node before the tree lock, so a `TX` holder does overlap another writer (matrix argument 1 is false) on PostgreSQL and MySQL/MariaDB. `PurgeTrashCommand.php:86` `lockTrashedRoot` (`NodeStoreRepository.php:201` `FOR UPDATE`) runs before `ForceDeleteNodeAction.php:52` `lockTree`. Restore does the opposite: `RestoreNodeAction.php:47` `lockTree`, then `:49` `FOR UPDATE` on the same node. Purge holds the node and waits for the tree lock; Restore holds the tree lock and waits for the node. Same cycle with Trash (`TrashNodeAction.php:44` then `:46`) and Move (`MoveNodeAction.php:53` then `:55`).

3. New-version upload never re-reads the target under the tree lock, so `used_bytes` drifts on every driver and a force-deleted node grows new blob edges. `previousHeadSize` and `assertWithinQuota` run at `UploadFileAction.php:78` and `:84`, outside the transaction; `:117` applies that stale delta. Two versions that both sampled `size_bytes = 100` and then commit 40 and 70 end at head 70 with `used_bytes` reduced by 90. Separately, ForceDelete can commit first (`ForceDeleteNodeAction.php:74` detaches edges, `:77` releases quota). The upload then `save()`s the soft-deleted row — Eloquent `save()` uses `newModelQuery()`, which does not apply the soft-delete scope — and `attach`s new edges (`:198`), so GC no longer reclaims the blob.

4. Copy records a stale size for a fresh head. `CopyNodeAction.php:57` keeps the caller's node; inside the transaction it locks only the destination (`:67`). `:110` and `:120` use that model's `size_bytes`, while `:140` and `:147` load the current file head from the database. A version that committed at 250 bytes after the model was loaded at 100 is copied as a 250-byte head on a node stamped 100, and `used_bytes` increases by 100. On PostgreSQL this also happens mid-copy: a new-version upload holds only `TS`, which copy already holds.
